I've been farming these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 20 years. I'm 48 now, finished middle school, then came straight back to the land. I've sat through a few village training meetings, but I learn more from watching my neighbors and from doing it myself.

My family has four people. My wife and I do most of the field work, but my son works in a factory in Handan and sends money home. That helps buy inputs, but it also means I have to hire two day-laborers at wheat harvest and maybe one at maize harvest, because we don't have enough hands.

Last year my wheat made about 950 jin per mu and the maize made about 1,100 jin. The wheat was a little disappointing — the neighbor to my east used an improved variety and got over 1,000 jin. I'm buying improved wheat seed again this year, probably Jimai 22 or whatever the county seed shop is pushing. For maize, I always buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar. I never save seed — my father tried that once and the yield dropped badly.

For fertilizer, I don't mess around. I put one bag of compound fertilizer on each mu of wheat before sowing — that's 50 kg per mu. The bag is the special wheat kind, around 16-16-8. That costs about 90 yuan. Then at green-up in March, I spread 20 kg urea on top, another 35 yuan. My neighbor cuts back on fertilizer to save money, but I think that's stupid — if I lose 100 jin of wheat, that's over 100 yuan gone. Better to put on a bit too much.

For maize, after wheat harvest in June I plant right away. No time to waste. I put 50 kg of the corn compound per mu at sowing — the kind with more nitrogen, about 22-10-8. Then when the corn is knee-high and the big bell is coming, I chase-fertilize with 15 kg urea. The dealer told me that pushes the ear big, and I've seen it work on my field.

Water: I pump from my well. Electricity keeps getting more expensive, so I count every time. For wheat I irrigate three times — the winter freezing water in late November, the green-up water in late March, and the jointing water in April. Three is enough if May brings a little rain. For maize, twice — once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out in July. The summer rains usually do the rest.

Pesticides: For wheat, I spray herbicide once in early spring when the wheat is still low, and once for aphids around the filling stage. That's two sprays. For maize, I spray herbicide once after emergence, and once for corn borer if I see the moths flying in July. Two sprays.

Tillage: Before wheat sowing in October, I hire the rotary tiller to break up the maize stubble. After wheat harvest in June, there is no time to plough deep — I direct-seed the maize no-till. Everyone around here does it that way now. The wheat stubble mulch helps keep moisture anyway.

I expect about 960 jin per mu from wheat and 1,100 jin per mu from maize if the weather doesn't turn bad.
